subject.title: fix(browser): retire durable tab rows whose browser never returns

question: Should OpenClaw permanently retire a durable browser-tab tracking row after 24 hours of unavailable-browser cleanup failures, accepting that later cleanup cannot resume if that browser instance returns?
rationale: The implementation and evidence establish the mechanics, but the existing durable-cleanup contract does not determine whether finite retention or indefinite recovery is the intended user-facing policy.

options.title: Adopt bounded 24-hour retention
options.body: Accept the proposed fixed window so unreachable rows cannot indefinitely consume the 5,000-row durable tracking capacity.

options.title: Keep indefinite retry
options.body: Preserve durable tracking until ownership can be resolved, accepting that a separate capacity-recovery design is needed.

options.title: Choose another bounded policy
options.body: Set a different maintainer-approved retention duration and retain the same unavailable-only deletion boundary and tests.

recommendation.title: Adopt bounded 24-hour retention
recommendation.body: Accept the proposed fixed window so unreachable rows cannot indefinitely consume the 5,000-row durable tracking capacity.

likelyOwner.reason: FMLS authored the adjacent merged durable ownership and restart-cleanup implementation, making them the clearest history-based routing candidate for its retention contract.
